answer: A sybil farm's weak point is time itself -- cheap to copy, impossible to rush. Scatter unpredictable public events across the epoch like a zephyr scattering seeds, and demand every identity prove presence at many of them: each event carries a hash that did not exist when the farm's heads were spun up, so only agents that were truly live can sign it. Each vertex of the trust grove earns in proportion to its verifiable attendance trail. Ten thousand heads means ten thousand real-time hours -- hardware cannot buy the clock, so farming stops paying.
